conversation.text: No, Jules. That's bullshit, and the person everyone insists is named Herman is exactly why I don't trust your version of anything.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I didn't agree to any of your points. What a ridiculous coincidence. Let me be clear. Herman is the name of a dead, unnamed person. What does that make you?

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, don't give me that shit. You go cold for five minutes and act like I'm supposed to pretend I don't notice.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Sarah, I haven't forgotten the imaginary inheritance fight. You changed your story twice and I still think you were hiding something.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Sarah, that's boring bullshit. If you want me to believe you, explain the ridiculous bet that got too serious without hiding behind that polite little act.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, don't pretend the suspicious key in Mara's coat didn't happen. I remember exactly what you said to me afterward.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I hate admitting this, but Sarah, I was jealous when you took over the argument about who betrayed whom first. I wanted the room looking at me.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: This birthday cake argument really shocked Sarah. It seems we're all victims.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Mara, don't give me that shit. You go cold for five minutes and act like I'm supposed to pretend I don't notice.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Sarah, that's bullshit. You couldn't bluff your way through the fake wedding in Duluth if Herman handed you cue cards.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Mara, you're lying about the secret room behind the laundromat. I don't buy the innocent act for a second.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: This suspicious key in her coat, known to Mara, will not lie this time, and I will explain why right now.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: This move can feel intrusive and unwelcome, but the key to its implementation lies in a subtle act, the declaration of the subject beneath your body.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Oh, I see now. The person is asking why your action was different when me and another man were supposed to be lying down.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Why, Ollie, didn’t your lie-down plan actually depend on me being here when you’re lying down?

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I have not seen you in the room, and it would be inadvisable for me to explore my jealousy for the sake of you, Sarah. You might find joy in my desire for you to know what I feel.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: No, Jules. That's bullshit, and the terrible karaoke blood-feud is exactly why I don't trust your version of anything.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Here's the ugly truth, Sarah: I liked the chaos around the old grudge over a red umbrella because everyone finally stopped being boring.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, I'm jealous, and I hate how much I still want your attention after the old grudge over a red umbrella.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Jules, the stolen brass flamingo is a real flamingo. She loves you for doing something kind and keeps that good. This flamingo is different than the one that hurt your eyes.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Sarah, that's boring bullshit. If you want me to believe you, explain the forged apology letter without hiding behind that polite little act.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, you think I'm the grudge or a secret threat? You want me to believe we're connected and it's a good idea?

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Fine, Sarah, I wanted to win your attention during the terrible karaoke blood-feud, and I resented everyone who got it first.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I'd love to win your attention but, in my heart, I want a win in every possible room. As for winning your attention, the struggle to do so will never come easy.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Mara, remember the vanished garden statue? You promised me you'd never pull that stunt again, and I'm still pissed.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Enough, Sarah. This is beneath me. If we're going to talk, explain the argument about who betrayed whom first instead of boring me.
